name: Prize crossword No 25,011
preamble: Nine clues contain no definition; their solutions have a connection.

clue.text: Conditional version of will is heard

indicators.note: something that is heard is taken in by the ear, so we want a word spelt differently but spoken the same

blocks.note: 'would' is the conditional form of the auxiliary 'will'

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on the conditional mood of the verb 'will'.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is the comedian Victoria Wood, and the preamble supplies the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Wood was a much-loved British comedian, writer and actress, linking this entry to the other eight themed solutions.

clue.text: Wall covering reduces rising carbon monoxide

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to reduce is to cut
CO is the chemical formula of carbon monoxide

explanation.surface: A plastered wall that somehow cuts down on carbon monoxide fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduces' looks like the verb linking definition to wordplay, but it supplies the reversed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster rendered onto exterior or interior walls as a protective and decorative coat.

clue.text: Result of clot grinding ribs smooth

indicators.note: grinding breaks something up and mixes it, so the letters are reworked into a fresh order

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Some odd medical claim that a blood clot can grind bones smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' could be an idiot, but here it is a blood clot and part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot forming inside a vessel and blocking blood flow is the medical condition this word names.

clue.text: Lie-abed heartlessly disturbed should go down OK

definitions.note: a phrase for an adjective: something fit to eat

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is dropped
disturbed things are thrown out of their settled order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the seven-letter word loses its middle letter A

explanation.surface: A lazy sleeper roused from bed is told everything will be all right.
explanation.walkthrough: A lie-abed is someone who stays late in bed. 'Should go down OK' reads as reassurance but means the food can safely be swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is safe to eat will be swallowed without harm, which is what fit for eating means.

clue.text: Duty keeps one in blue moving pictures

indicators.note: to keep is to hold onto, so the outer word wraps around the rest
placing something in another sets it inside, before the mix
moving letters around shifts them into a new order

blocks.note: a tax is a duty levied by government
one as the article 'a'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tax slapped on a sad person going to the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving pictures' looks like the definition (films), but 'moving' is the anagram signal and only 'pictures' defines. The mixed letters sit between TA and X.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableaux are striking scenes or arranged groups, as in tableaux vivants, staged pictures formed by posed people.

clue.text: Sporting event stopped being without fixed limits

blocks.note: an Open is a tournament anyone may enter, such as golf's Open Championship
stopped as in came to an end

explanation.surface: A sports fixture is called off because it had no rules about duration.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces sit side by side in order; the hyphen joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no predetermined conclusion or boundary is unrestricted, the sense the compound adjective carries.

clue.text: Fuss when bishop mounts our makeshift, unobtrusive barrier

indicators.note: a makeshift thing is improvised, cobbled together in whatever order comes to hand
in a down entry, to mount is to sit on top, so this letter comes first

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
taken as written
a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a fence without spoiling the view

explanation.surface: A cleric climbs over a hastily built fence and causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a landscaping feature on English country estates: a ditch with a wall on one side that keeps livestock out without blocking the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or outcry over something, which is a synonym for a fuss.

clue.text: Chasing women, nobody excluded!

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
if nobody is left out, everybody is included

explanation.surface: A womaniser who chases every woman without exception.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is the comedian Max Wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Wall was a British music-hall comedian famous for his silly walks, so he joins the other eight themed comics.

clue.text: Expression of delight in art deco wrought figures

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so these letters are hammered into a new form
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a cry of pleasure
seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sighing with pleasure at the wrought-metal shapes of an Art Deco design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art deco wrought figures' reads as one phrase about metalwork, but 'wrought' is the anagram signal and 'figures' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Octahedra are solid geometric shapes with eight faces, so in mathematics they are figures.

clue.text: Regimental man taking centre from smoking jacket

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it, so the outer word grips a letter
the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: a para is a soldier of the Parachute Regiment
the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: An army officer borrowing the middle of someone's smoking jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoking jacket' is a familiar phrase, but 'smoking' only lends its middle letter and 'jacket' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded, padded windproof coat, an outer garment of the jacket kind.

clue.text: Garland: love casual look

blocks.note: to garland is to deck with flowers
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A florist's quick glance at a lover's wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garland' looks like a noun but works as a verb meaning to adorn. Decko (also dekko) is British slang, from army Hindi.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a dekko means having a quick glance, an informal slang term for a brief look.

clue.text: Two-tongued iguana bats, no tail, having divided beak

indicators.note: a word with no tail has lost its final letter
bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order
something that has divided another has split it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: a bird's bill is its beak
the reptile loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A lizard with a forked tongue, flying bats and a split beak: a weird menagerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-tongued' suggests a forked lizard tongue, but tongue here means language. 'Bats' is an adjective meaning mad, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an old word for language, so someone with two tongues speaks two languages fluently.

clue.text: Be splattered with micro material

indicators.note: something splattered is scattered messily, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning about getting splashed with some tiny particles.
explanation.walkthrough: Crombie is a Scottish woollen cloth, and the overcoat made of it, named after the mill that wove it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crombie is a brand of heavy woollen fabric, so it is a textile or cloth, a kind of material.

clue.text: Horse artist's a hooded killer

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard artist

explanation.surface: A painter of horses who is secretly a masked murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooded killer' sounds like an executioner or assassin, but the hood is the flared neck of a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The snake spreads a hood of ribs behind its head when threatened, and its venomous bite can kill.

clue.text: About to invade a controversial composer's area

indicators.note: an invader gets inside territory, so this piece lands within another

blocks.note: taken as written
John Cage, whose silent piece 4'33" still divides opinion
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone moving into a divisive composer's patch of territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The piece meaning about goes inside CAGE, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is land measured in acres, so it is used for an extent or expanse of ground.

clue.text: Crack in brick tile construction over river

indicators.note: a construction is something built up from parts, so the letters are assembled anew
in a down entry, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A builder spots a fissure in the brickwork of a bridge spanning a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack in brick' looks like a structural fault, but a crack is also a wisecrack, a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack can mean a witty remark or gag, and a rib-tickler is a very funny joke.

clue.text: See 6
Sailors trapped in overturned vessel

indicators.note: turning something over puts it the other way round, so the letters run backwards
whatever is trapped sits inside its captor

blocks.note: a sub, a submarine, is a vessel
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A crew stuck inside a capsized boat.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is the comedian George Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: George Burns was an American comedian of vaudeville, radio and film, joining the other eight themed comics.

clue.text: They hate getting iffy silver after gutless contest

indicators.note: something iffy is dubious or unsound, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order
without guts means the inner letters are removed
coming after means following, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: a race with its inside letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Losers who resent winning a dodgy silver medal in a cowardly race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They hate' is a short clause standing for a plural noun: those who hate and abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Revilers are people who abuse or denounce others with scorn, so they are haters of a kind.

clue.text: Western American hacker

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
the American spelling of axe, a hacking tool

explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is Ruby Wax. 'Hacker' looks like a computer intruder but is a chopping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby Wax is an American-born comedian working in British television, joining the other eight themed comics.

clue.text: Clothes store with a border around

indicators.note: letters moved around are turned about into a different order

blocks.note: W is short for with
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clothes shop with a decorative edging running round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes store' reads as a shop, but it is a cupboard where clothes are stored.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a tall cupboard for hanging and keeping garments, literally a place to store clothes.

clue.text: Underwear and skimpy dress (just the top)

indicators.note: skimpy means scanty, so only a scrap of the garment is used
only the top of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a bra is an item of underwear
'n' is the clipped form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
the first letter

explanation.surface: A daring outfit: lingerie under a revealing dress, showing only the top.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is Russell Brand. 'And' gives N, as in fish 'n' chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Russell Brand is a British stand-up comedian and presenter, joining the other eight themed comics.

clue.text: Ives composed in the care of a doctor (consultant)

indicators.note: to compose is to arrange parts into a new piece, so the letters are rearranged
someone in the care of others is held within their keeping

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: The composer Charles Ives writing music while under a hospital consultant's care.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ives was an American composer, so 'composed' seems to describe him. A consultant is also a senior hospital doctor, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a professional who gives expert counsel, which is exactly the job of an adviser.

clue.text: Mobile plant that installs repetitive tune in the instruments' data openings

indicators.note: to install something is to put it in place inside, so one piece goes within another
the opening of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letters of three words
a riff is a short repeated musical phrase

explanation.surface: A technical note about recording a looping melody into instrument data channels.
explanation.walkthrough: Triffids are the walking, stinging plants of John Wyndham's novel The Day of the Triffids, so 'mobile' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyndham's fictional triffids uproot themselves and walk about, making them plants that can move around.

clue.text: Thanks to rap, one's "tropical paradise"?

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks
a rap is a sharp blow
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rapper thanking his music for his luxury island lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' suggests the music genre, but it is a knock. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is a South Pacific island of French Polynesia, a famous example of an idyllic tropical holiday spot.

clue.text: Father charms (but not workers)

indicators.note: but not means excepting, so these letters are taken away

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for a priest's title Father
to charm is to enchant
worker ants are the crossword's standard workers

explanation.surface: A priest who wins people over, though not the labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is the comedian Dawn French.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn French is a British comic actress, half of French and Saunders, joining the other eight themed comics.

clue.text: Lecture, as certain Scottish banks do

blocks.note: first meaning: to speak at length, pompously
second meaning, taken literally: the banks of a Scottish river contain its water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests the Royal Bank of Scotland and the like, but these are riverbanks. The Forth is the river flowing past Stirling into the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold forth is an idiom for talking at length in a pompous way, much as one delivers a lecture.

clue.text: Hard and evil

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
ill as in harm or wickedness

explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is the comedian Harry Hill. The 'and' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Hill is a British comedian known for big collars and TV Burp, joining the other eight themed comics.

clue.text: Cable once put under floor

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting a piece under another places it lower, so second

blocks.note: fl. is the abbreviation for floor
ex means former, what once was

explanation.surface: An electrician who used to run wiring beneath the floorboards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' looks like an adverb of time in the surface, but it supplies the prefix for former.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a flex is the insulated flexible electric lead on an appliance, a kind of cable.

clue.text: Shakespeare's fat? Awful cheek!

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone calls Shakespeare fat and is told off for impudence.
explanation.walkthrough: Keech is an archaic word for a lump of animal fat, used in Henry VIII and Henry IV Part 2.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare a keech is a rolled lump of tallow from a butcher, so it is fat in his vocabulary.

clue.text: Parking in garden

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to garden is to work the soil, to hoe
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Leaving a car on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is the comedian Bob Hope. 'Garden' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Hope was a British-born American comedian and film star, joining the other eight themed comics.

clue.text: Getting rid of sun's solar gels

indicators.note: getting rid of letters means removing them from the string

blocks.note: Sol is the sun; with the 's these are the letters taken away, two from each end
with SO gone from the front and LS from the back, the middle five letters are what is left

explanation.surface: Throwing out sunscreen gels after a day in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the nine themed clues with no definition: the answer is Eddie Large. SO goes from the front and LS from the back of the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Large was the larger half of the British comedy double act Little and Large, joining the other themed comics.

clue.text: Plant making goat cheese initially on a high?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: a goat is something that butts
the first letter
up means elated, in high spirits

explanation.surface: A farmyard plant used to make goat's cheese, apparently mind-altering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goat cheese' reads as one thing, but the goat is a butter, an animal that butts with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow-flowered meadow plant of the genus Ranunculus, a specific example of a plant.
